summary: Two-way alignment is stronger than periodic regeneration because it makes disagreement actionable. It must be implemented as typed reconciliation with provenance and review, not as unrestricted synchronization.

points.text: Define authority per field and artifact type: code may own deployed behavior, an ADR may own rationale, an API specification may own contract, and runtime telemetry may own observations. No universal last writer should win.
Each proposed update needs a stable entity ID, source and target revisions, transformation version, evidence links, owner, and idempotency key so retries do not create duplicate changes.
Semantic disagreement should enter a conflict queue. Automatically overwriting one side erases precisely the drift information the pattern is meant to surface.
Measure stale-link rate, reconciliation latency, false links, accepted versus rejected write-backs, conflict age, and rework; page freshness alone can hide wrong synchronization.
